answer: Each identity locks a 60-credit bond and seals each claim in a walnut ledger with a key-bound ember mark. Two conflicting claims for one slot from one key prove equivocation: the bond burns and the nectar pool bars the identity. One fake costs 95, 60 at risk plus 35 to craft a claim; the k-th fake costs the same 95, so 1,000 fakes cost 95,000, as ember marks are single-use and key-bound. A single-operator ring fails: signing for many identities creates conflicting claims, and the walnut ledger burns all linked bonds. An honest worker risks only the 60 bond, returned while clean.
